messages:
devon-customer: Hey team — we noticed a big billing spike this morning and users are getting intermittent 401s on our Private endpoint. Happened around 08:14 UTC. Any quick checks we can run?

sarah-support: sorry to hear that, devon. Can you share a failing request id / example curl and the x-request-id from the response? That helps us trace in the serving logs.

devon-customer: here's a minimal repro we captured from a client behind corp-proxy. It fails ~30% of requests with 401.

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://private-acme.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

Response snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 08:14:17 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: 1c9f4a2b-5d3f-4a2a-9e2a-6b7f1b2c3d4e

{"error":"unauthorized","message":"missing auth"}
```

sarah-support: thanks — nice and concrete. matt, can you start looking for that request id in the Private control plane/collector logs? Also, do we have any recent rollout that could affect header handling or our front proxy?

matt-eng: looking now. If the response shows "missing auth" it can be either (a) Authorization header is stripped by upstream proxy, (b) collector forward logic dropped it when doing internal requests, or (c) a timing/rotation issue with the token provider. First step: gather a debug bundle from the customer's collector host (includes collector logs, nginx/haproxy access logs, systemd journal, and network capture).

sarah-support: devon, I can walk you through generating a debug bundle. If you're comfortable, run the collector debug helper with no redaction so we can see headers. We will treat the bundle as sensitive and you can upload it to our SFTP dropbox. Command: 

```
sudo /opt/redwood/collector debug-bundle generate \
  --include-logs /var/log/redwood/collector.log \
  --include-systemd --include-proxy-logs /var/log/nginx/access.log \
  --include-network-capture --no-redact \
  --output /tmp/acme-debug-1734567899.tar.gz
```
Note: --no-redact will keep Authorization headers in the capture. Only run if you consent to share it with support.

devon-customer: we can do that, but our security team blocks outbound S3/HTTPS to unknown hosts. We can SFTP to a support account though. How should we transfer?

ops-bot: @sarah-support I created a temporary SFTP dropbox for tenant-acme: sftp://support-drop.redwood.example/acme-uploads/ (expires in 72h). Credentials sent to devon via secure DM.

sarah-support: perfect. After you generate the bundle, please scp/sftp to the dropbox path. If the transfer fails, paste the scp verbose output here.

devon-customer: generating now — will include nginx configs. One quick note: we run an internal edge proxy (corp-proxy) that rewrites long headers. Could be related.

matt-eng: if corp-proxy is rewriting headers, look for patterns in nginx access logs — sometimes a behavior triggers header truncation for large request bodies. Also check for repeated 401s tied to token rotation (we log token validation failures in collector auth module).

devon-customer: bundle generated: /tmp/acme-debug-1734567899.tar.gz. Upload attempt via sftp successful. Response from sftp client: "Upload complete, 87MB".

bundle-bot: New debug bundle uploaded: acme-uploads/acme-debug-1734567899.tar.gz (uploaded by devon-customer). Ticket ref: SUP-7543.

sarah-support: got it, thanks. We'll pull and start a private analysis pass. Matt — can you grep the collector logs for 1c9f4a2b-5d3f-4a2a-9e2a-6b7f1b2c3d4e and also look for sequences where Authorization header is present in client-facing logs but absent in internal requests?

matt-eng: on it. Quick findings: in the collector access log there are matching requests with that x-request-id, and I see an upstream proxy response code 401 with a note "auth header missing". In the nginx access log on the host, the incoming request contains Authorization. But when the collector forwards to the control plane, the Authorization header is not present in the forwarded request. Excerpt from collector.log: 

```
2025-06-23T08:14:17Z INFO request id=1c9f4a2b forward to controlplane status=401 reason="missing auth"
2025-06-23T08:14:17Z DEBUG outbound-headers id=1c9f4a2b headers="[X-Request-Id, X-Forwarded-For]"
```
Looks like our forwarder is intentionally whitelisting a small set of headers and Authorization isn't on the list. That would explain missing auth.

sarah-support: whoa — is that a recent config change? We do have a patch that tightened header whitelisting for privacy reasons rolled out last week. It may have been too strict for Private setups.

matt-eng: checking rollout notes... yes, commit 9f3c2a added a default header whitelist. Private collectors should inherit a config flag to preserve Authorization, but looks like devon's tenant config didn't set it. Two remediation options: (1) enable header preserve on that collector and ask customer to redeploy collector (fast), or (2) update forwarder to add Authorization by default for Private tenants (requires QA).

sarah-support: for now let's get them unblocked: devon, can you set /etc/redwood/collector/config.yaml add: 

```
forwarder:
  preserve_incoming_headers: ["Authorization", "X-Custom-Auth"]
```

Then restart collector: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-collector`. After restart, please reproduce the failing request and post new x-request-id.

devon-customer: will do. Restarting... reproducing now. New response: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-Id: 9a8b7c6d-2e1f-4b1a-b2c3-d4e5f6789012

Great — after the config change it looks resolved. Billing spike probably caused by repeated token churn while the Authorization was failing.

matt-eng: great news. We'll follow up with a config patch to set preserve_incoming_headers for Private by default (and add a migration).

sarah-support: thanks everyone — closing the immediate customer impact. We'll keep SUP-7543 open to track the config default and a note to add a regression test. @devon-customer if you prefer, we can rotate any tokens that were used during the window.

devon-customer: yes please rotate the affected API key. Thanks for the quick help :rocket: 

sarah-support: noted, initiating key rotation and follow-up postmortem. :thumbsup:
